title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 70 (Prohibition of buy-back in certain cases)

content.overview: Section 70 prohibits direct or indirect buy-back through a subsidiary or an investment company/group of investment companies; bars buy-back after specified repayment/dividend/loan defaults unless the default is remedied and three years have elapsed after it ceased; and separately bars buy-back if sections 92, 123, 127 and 129 have not been complied with.
content.glance: Section 70 prohibits direct or indirect buy-back through a subsidiary or an investment company/group of investment companies; bars buy-back after specified repayment/dividend/loan defaults unless the default is remedied and three years have elapsed after it ceased; and separately bars buy-back if sections 92, 123, 127 and 129 have not been complied with.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 70 (Prohibition for buy-back in certain circumstances). A company must not directly or indirectly buy back its own shares or specified securities through a subsidiary company, including its own subsidiary companies, or through an investment company or group of investment companies. A buy-back is also barred where the company has defaulted in repayment of deposits or interest, redemption of debentures or preference shares, payment of dividend to a shareholder, or repayment of a term loan or interest payable to a financial institution or banking company. The proviso permits buy-back only if the default is remedied and three years have elapsed after the default ceased to subsist. Separately, subsection (2) bars buy-back if the company has not complied with sections 92, 123, 127 and 129. These restrictions supplement, and do not replace, the conditions in section 68.

sections.heading: Subsidiary and investment-company routes
sections.body: A company must not directly or indirectly buy back its own shares or specified securities through a subsidiary company, including its own subsidiary companies, or through an investment company or group of investment companies.

sections.heading: Specified defaults and three-year period
sections.body: A buy-back is barred where default has been made in repayment of deposits or interest, redemption of debentures or preference shares, payment of dividend to any shareholder, or repayment of a term loan or interest payable to a financial institution or banking company. The proviso permits buy-back only after the default is remedied and three years have elapsed after it ceased to subsist.

sections.heading: Compliance with other provisions
sections.body: Subsection (2) separately prohibits buy-back where the company has not complied with sections 92, 123, 127 and 129.

sections.heading: Relationship with section 68
sections.body: Section 70 states additional prohibitions. Meeting the general buy-back conditions in section 68 does not remove a prohibition under section 70.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 70: Prohibition for buy-back in certain circumstances

examples.title: Buy-back bars
examples.body: Section 70 bars buy-back through a subsidiary or investment company, and bars buy-back while a default in repayment of deposits, redemption of preference shares or debentures, or payment of dividend remains uncured.

hypotheticals.question: A company repays a term-loan default and wants to buy back shares one year later. Is the default proviso satisfied?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The proviso requires the default to be remedied and three years to have elapsed after it ceased to subsist. The other section 70 conditions and section 68 must also be checked.

hypotheticals.question: A company has not complied with section 129 but has no repayment defaults. Can it proceed with buy-back?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 70(2) separately bars buy-back if the company has not complied with section 129, even if no subsection (1)(c) repayment default exists.

distinctions.title: Buy-back conditions and prohibitions
distinctions.left: Section 68 states the general power and conditions for buy-back.
distinctions.right: Section 70 imposes additional prohibitions that can prevent buy-back despite compliance with section 68.

rows.right: Cure plus three years; also compliance with sections 92, 123, 127 and 129

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the buy-back bar ends immediately when a repayment default is cured.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso requires both cure and the passage of three years after the default ceased to subsist.

misconceptions.trap: Checking only section 68 and ignoring section 70(2).
misconceptions.correction: Section 70 separately bars buy-back for non-compliance with sections 92, 123, 127 and 129.

misconceptions.trap: Treating only a direct purchase by the company as covered.
misconceptions.correction: Section 70 also addresses specified indirect routes through subsidiaries and investment companies.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the three-year rule under section 70?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Where a specified default has occurred, the buy-back prohibition is lifted under the proviso only if the default is remedied and three years have elapsed after it ceased to subsist.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Which other statutory compliance does section 70(2) require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The company must have complied with sections 92, 123, 127 and 129.
